packs.name: Devotional and contemplative
packs.about: F. B. Meyer’s daily readings, with seven classics of prayer: à Kempis, Brother Lawrence, Teresa, John of the Cross, Julian, Augustine and The Cloud of Unknowing.

packs.name: Commentaries
packs.about: Hastings’ Great Texts of the Bible: expositions full of illustration.

packs.name: Greek word studies
packs.about: Robertson’s Word Pictures (Matthew to Paul’s letters) and Vincent’s Word Studies.

packs.name: History and background
packs.about: Edersheim’s Life and Times of Jesus the Messiah.

packs.name: Study notes
packs.about: Tyndale Open Study Notes (2022): modern study notes on every book, with theme articles, profiles of Bible people and book introductions. Openly licensed (CC BY-SA 4.0).

packs.name: Bible dictionary
packs.about: Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary (2023): articles on the people, places, customs and ideas of the Bible. Openly licensed (CC BY-SA 4.0).

packs.name: Maclaren’s Expositions
packs.about: Alexander Maclaren, Expositions of Holy Scripture (1904–10): about 1,200 sermons and expositions from Genesis to 1 John, by the “prince of expository preachers”. Warm, clear and practical.

packs.name: The Expositor’s Bible
packs.about: The Expositor’s Bible (ed. W. Robertson Nicoll, 1887–1905): readable book-by-book expositions by Marcus Dods, George Adam Smith, James Denney, Alexander Maclaren and others, covering most of the Bible.

sources.author: A. T. Robertson
sources.work: Word Pictures in the New Testament
sources.credit: A. T. Robertson, Word Pictures in the New Testament, vols. 1–4 (Richard R. Smith, 1930–31). Public domain. Text from the CrossWire SWORD module RWP. Volumes 5–6 (John, Hebrews, the General Epistles, Revelation) are left out while still in US copyright.
sources.caveat: Greek is printed without accents and occasionally drops a final letter; explain the word rather than copying the Greek exactly. Robertson's grammar is solid; some textual and historical judgements are a century old.

sources.author: Marvin R. Vincent
sources.work: Word Studies in the New Testament
sources.credit: Marvin R. Vincent, Word Studies in the New Testament, 4 vols. (Charles Scribner’s Sons, 1887–1900; this printing 1900–01). Public domain. Scanned text from archive.org (Princeton Theological Seminary Library).
sources.caveat: Scanned text: the Greek words in it are often garbled by the scan, so never quote Greek from Vincent; use his English explanations. A few notes may be tagged to a neighbouring verse.

sources.author: F. B. Meyer
sources.work: Through the Bible Day by Day
sources.credit: F. B. Meyer, Through the Bible Day by Day, vols. I, II and IV–VII (American Sunday-School Union, 1914–18). Public domain. Scanned text from archive.org.
sources.caveat: Written for daily devotion in 1914–18; warm and direct, and of its time on some questions.

sources.author: James Hastings (ed.)
sources.work: The Great Texts of the Bible
sources.credit: James Hastings (ed.), The Great Texts of the Bible, 20 vols. (T. & T. Clark; Charles Scribner’s Sons, 1910–15). Public domain. Scanned text from archive.org.
sources.caveat: Edwardian preaching, rich in illustration and quotation from other writers; some views of science, society and other faiths are of their time. Quotations inside it are from the writers Hastings cites, so name them when you use them.

sources.author: Thomas à Kempis
sources.credit: Thomas à Kempis, The Imitation of Christ, translated by William Benham (1886). Public domain. Scanned text from archive.org.

sources.author: Brother Lawrence
sources.work: The Practice of the Presence of God
sources.credit: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God: conversations and letters (Fleming H. Revell, 1895). Public domain. Scanned text from archive.org.

sources.author: Teresa of Ávila
sources.credit: Teresa of Ávila, The Interior Castle, or The Mansions, translated by the Benedictines of Stanbrook, revised by Benedict Zimmerman, 3rd ed. (Thomas Baker, 1921). Public domain in the US. Scanned text from archive.org.
sources.caveat: The scan lost the Second Mansions.

sources.author: John of the Cross
sources.work: The Dark Night of the Soul
sources.credit: John of the Cross, The Dark Night of the Soul, translated by David Lewis, 4th ed. revised by Benedict Zimmerman (Thomas Baker, 1916). Public domain in the US. Scanned text from archive.org.

sources.author: Julian of Norwich
sources.credit: Julian of Norwich, Revelations of Divine Love, edited by Grace Warrack (Methuen, 1901). Public domain. Scanned text from archive.org.

sources.author: Augustine of Hippo
sources.credit: Augustine, Confessions, translated by E. B. Pusey (Oxford, 1838). Public domain. Scanned text from archive.org.

sources.author: The Cloud of Unknowing
sources.credit: The Cloud of Unknowing, edited by Evelyn Underhill, 2nd ed. (John M. Watkins, 1922). Public domain in the US. Scanned text from archive.org.
sources.caveat: Middle English lightly modernised by Underhill; some words are archaic.

sources.author: Alfred Edersheim
sources.work: The Life and Times of Jesus the Messiah
sources.credit: Alfred Edersheim, The Life and Times of Jesus the Messiah, 2 vols., 8th ed. (Longmans, Green, 1899; first published 1883). Public domain. Scanned text from archive.org (University of Toronto).
sources.caveat: Written in 1883. Edersheim often reads later rabbinic writings (the Talmud and Midrash, compiled centuries after Jesus) back into first-century practice, and some of his judgements about Judaism reflect his time; say so when drawing on him for Jewish custom.

sources.author: Tyndale House Publishers
sources.credit: Tyndale Open Study Notes, © 2022 Tyndale House Publishers, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Adapted from Tyndale Open Study Notes: formatting removed and short notes grouped by chapter. The original work by Tyndale House Publishers is available for free at http://www.tyndaleopenresources.com.
sources.caveat: Modern evangelical study notes keyed to the New Living Translation: phrases they quote from the passage are NLT wording, which can differ from the World English Bible text being studied.

sources.author: Tyndale House Publishers
sources.credit: Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary, © 2023 Tyndale House Publishers, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0). Adapted from Tyndale Open Bible Dictionary: formatting, pictures and maps removed. The original work by Tyndale House Publishers is available for free at http://www.tyndaleopenresources.com.
sources.caveat: A Bible dictionary keyed to the New Living Translation: names and quoted phrases follow the NLT, which can differ from the World English Bible.

sources.author: Alexander Maclaren
sources.credit: Alexander Maclaren, Expositions of Holy Scripture (Hodder & Stoughton; A. C. Armstrong, 1904–10). Public domain. Text from Project Gutenberg’s editions.
sources.caveat: Victorian sermons preached in Manchester, quoting the Authorised (King James) Version. Their warmth and turns of phrase are Maclaren’s own: draw on his insight in fresh words, and quote only a short phrase where it is memorable.

sources.author: W. Robertson Nicoll (ed.)
sources.credit: The Expositor’s Bible, edited by W. Robertson Nicoll, by various authors (Hodder & Stoughton; A. C. Armstrong, 1887–1905): the 49 volumes in Project Gutenberg’s editions. Public domain.
sources.caveat: Late-Victorian scholarship, each volume by a different writer (named with each passage). Some critical views (dates, authorship) reflect debates of the 1890s; give the writer’s name with any view that may be dated.
